drivingQuestion: From where do we know that a son precedes a daughter in inheriting the father?
outcomeNote: Rav Pappa's challenge is taken up in the next unit.

segments.he: וְהַבָּנִים אֶת הָאָב. מְנָלַן? דִּכְתִיב: ״אִישׁ כִּי יָמוּת וְגוֹ׳״. טַעְמָא דְּאֵין לוֹ בֵּן, הָא יֵשׁ לוֹ בֵּן – בֵּן קוֹדֵם. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי, אֵימָא: אִי אִיכָּא בֵּן – לֵירוֹת בֵּן, אִיכָּא בַּת – תֵּירוֹת בַּת, אִיכָּא בֵּן וּבַת – לָא הַאי לֵירוֹת וְלָא הַאי לֵירוֹת!
segments.en: § The mishna teaches in the list of those who inherit from and bequeath to each other: «Sons» with regard to «their father.» The Gemara asks: «From where do we» derive this halakha that sons inherit the entire estate and daughters do not receive a share along with them? «As it is written: “If a man dies,» and has no son, then you shall pass his inheritance to his daughter” (Numbers 27:8). «The reason» the inheritance would be passed to a daughter is «that he has no son, but» if «he has a son,» the «son takes precedence. Rav Pappa said to Abaye:» Why not «say» the following: «If there is» only «a son, let» the «son inherit» the father’s estate; if «there is» only «a daughter, let» the «daughter inherit» the father’s estate; and if «there is» both «a son and a daughter, neither this one should inherit nor that one should inherit.»
